description: Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, is a beloved Indian curry known for its rich, creamy tomato-based sauce and tender pieces of marinated chicken. This iconic dish offers a perfect balance of sweet, tangy, and subtly spicy flavors, making it a comforting and incredibly satisfying meal. It's a true classic that brings the authentic taste of India right to your dining table.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: Combine chicken pieces with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, red chili powder, turmeric, garam masala, and salt in a bowl. Mix well, cover, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours for best flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Marinated Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of ghee or butter in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken in batches, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook until browned and mostly cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per batch. Remove cooked chicken and set aside.

instructions.title: Sauté Aromatics for the Sauce
instructions.text: In the same pan, add the remaining 1 tablespoon of ghee or butter. Add the finely chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Build the Makhani Sauce Base
instructions.text: Add green cardamom pods, cinnamon stick, and bay leaf to the pan. Stir in red chili powder, coriander powder, and cumin powder. Cook for 30 seconds until aromatic. Pour in the crushed tomatoes and the soaked cashews (drained). Bring the mixture to a simmer, then cover and cook for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes are well cooked and the oil starts to separate.

instructions.title: Blend the Sauce to Smoothness
instructions.text: Remove the bay leaf, cinnamon stick, and cardamom pods (if easily found). Carefully transfer the sauce mixture to a blender and blend until completely smooth and creamy. You may need to add a splash of water or chicken broth if the sauce is too thick. For an extra velvety texture, pass the blended sauce through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan.

instructions.title: Combine and Finish the Curry
instructions.text: Return the cooked chicken to the smooth sauce. Stir in the garam masala, sugar, and salt to taste. Simmer for 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the chicken to finish cooking through. Finally, stir in the heavy cream and the crushed Kasoori Methi. Heat gently for 2-3 minutes; do not boil after adding cream as it can curdle.

instructions.title: Serve Your Butter Chicken
instructions.text: Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro. Serve your authentic Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani hot with warm naan bread, roti, or fluffy basmati rice for a truly satisfying Indian lunch.

tips: For an extra creamy and rich sauce, ensure your cashews are soaked in hot water for at least 15-20 minutes before blending. This helps them achieve a super smooth consistency.

Always toast your Kasoori Methi (dried fenugreek leaves) lightly in a dry pan for about 30 seconds before crushing them between your palms and adding to the sauce. This simple step unlocks their full aromatic potential.
When adding heavy cream, keep the heat on low and do not bring the curry to a rolling boil afterwards, as this can cause the cream to curdle. Gently warm it through to maintain a smooth texture.
article:
Craving a taste of India that's rich, creamy, and utterly satisfying? Look no further than Butter Chicken, known in Hindi as Murgh Makhani. This iconic dish has captured hearts worldwide with its velvety tomato-based sauce, tender chicken, and delicate balance of spices. While often enjoyed in restaurants, mastering an authentic Indian Butter Chicken Recipe at home is incredibly rewarding. Perfect for a comforting lunch or a special dinner, Butter Chicken is a culinary masterpiece that’s surprisingly accessible to prepare. Get ready to embark on a flavorful journey and bring the magic of Indian cuisine into your kitchen.

## What is Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)?
Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, literally translates to "chicken with butter." Originating in Delhi, India, in the 1950s, it's a relatively modern classic born from the culinary innovations of the Moti Mahal restaurant. The story goes that leftover tandoori chicken was simmered in a rich tomato gravy, creating a dish that quickly became a sensation. What defines Murgh Makhani is its signature creamy, mildly spiced, and slightly sweet tomato sauce, enriched with butter, cream, and often cashews or almonds for thickness. Unlike spicier curries, Butter Chicken offers a gentle warmth, making it incredibly appealing to a wide palate, including those new to Indian food. It’s a celebration of textures and flavors, where succulent pieces of marinated chicken are enveloped in a luxurious, aromatic sauce.

## Ingredients for Indian Butter Chicken
To create this beloved Indian Butter Chicken Recipe, you'll need a selection of fresh, high-quality ingredients. Don't be intimidated by the list; each component plays a crucial role in building the depth of flavor.

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast, cut into bite-sized pieces
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri for color, or regular for heat)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   Salt to taste
*   1 tablespoon lemon juice

For the Makhani (Butter) Sauce:
*   2 tablespoons butter (plus extra for finishing)
*   1 tablespoon oil
*   2 large onions, finely chopped
*   2 tablespoons ginger-garlic paste
*   1 (800g) can crushed tomatoes or 6-7 fresh ripe tomatoes, pureed
*   1/2 cup cashews (soaked in warm water for 15-20 minutes, then pureed)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1 teaspoon ground cumin
*   1 teaspoon ground coriander
*   1/2 teaspoon fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi), crushed
*   1/2 cup heavy cream
*   1-2 tablespoons sugar (or to taste, balances acidity)
*   Salt to taste
*   Fresh cilantro, chopped (for garnish)

## Step-by-Step Guide to Making Butter Chicken
Preparing this delightful Indian Butter Chicken Recipe is a journey of layering flavors. Follow these steps for a truly authentic experience.

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** In a large bowl, combine all ingredients for the chicken marinade. Add the chicken pieces, ensuring they are thoroughly coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, or even overnight for maximum flavor and tenderness.
2.  **Cook the Chicken:** Heat a tablespoon of oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken in batches, cooking until browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per batch. Remove the cooked chicken and set aside. It doesn't need to be fully cooked through at this stage, as it will finish cooking in the sauce.
3.  **Prepare the Sauce Base:** In the same pan, melt 2 tablespoons of butter and a tablespoon of oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and sauté until translucent and lightly golden, about 8-10 minutes. Add the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.
4.  **Add Tomatoes and Spices:** Stir in the pureed tomatoes, soaked and pureed cashews, turmeric powder, red chili powder, garam masala, ground cumin, and ground coriander. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 10-15 minutes, allowing the sauce to thicken and the oil to separate from the sides. This step is crucial for developing deep flavor.
5.  **Simmer the Sauce:** If desired, for an extra smooth sauce, carefully blend the mixture with an immersion blender or transfer to a regular blender and blend until completely smooth. Return the sauce to the pan. Add about 1/2 to 1 cup of water or chicken broth to achieve your desired consistency. Bring to a gentle simmer.
6.  **Combine and Finish:** Add the cooked chicken back into the sauce. Stir in the crushed kasoori methi, heavy cream, sugar, and salt to taste. Let it simmer gently for another 5-10 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the chicken to absorb the richness of the sauce. Before serving, stir in an extra knob of butter for that classic "butter" finish and garnish generously with fresh cilantro.

## Pro Tips for the Best Murgh Makhani
Elevate your Indian Butter Chicken Recipe from good to extraordinary with these expert tips:

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skip or shorten the marination time. The yogurt and lemon juice tenderize the chicken and infuse it with flavor, making a significant difference in the final dish's texture and taste. Overnight marination is highly recommended.
*   **Quality Ingredients:** Use fresh, ripe tomatoes or high-quality canned crushed tomatoes. Fresh ginger-garlic paste made at home provides a more vibrant flavor than store-bought. Similarly, fresh cream and good quality butter make a noticeable impact on the sauce's richness.
*   **Bloom Your Spices:** When adding powdered spices to the sauce, cook them briefly with the onions and ginger-garlic paste before adding tomatoes. This "blooming" process in oil releases their aromatic compounds and deepens their flavor.
*   **Achieve Silky Smoothness:** For an ultra-smooth restaurant-style sauce, after cooking the tomatoes and spices, blend the sauce base thoroughly. You can also pass it through a fine-mesh sieve to remove any remaining solids for an incredibly luxurious texture.
*   **Balance Flavors:** Taste your sauce frequently. Butter Chicken thrives on a balance of sweet, tangy, and savory. Adjust sugar and salt as needed. A little extra butter or a touch more cream at the end can enhance the richness without overpowering. Kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves) is essential; it provides a unique, slightly bitter, and aromatic depth that is characteristic of authentic Murgh Makhani.

## Serving Suggestions for Butter Chicken
The beauty of this classic Indian Butter Chicken Recipe lies not just in its taste but also in its versatility as a centerpiece for an Indian meal. Traditionally, it's served alongside warm, fluffy **Naan bread** or **Garlic Naan**, which is perfect for scooping up every last bit of that luscious sauce. Alternatively, **Basmati rice**, cooked plain or as a fragrant pilaf, provides a wonderful contrast, soaking up the creamy gravy beautifully. For a complete meal, consider adding a side of cooling **Cucumber Raita** (yogurt dip), which offers a refreshing counterpoint to the richness of the curry. A simple **Kachumber salad** (diced cucumber, tomato, onion with lemon and cilantro) also adds a fresh, zesty crunch. Don't forget a sprinkle of fresh cilantro for garnish to brighten the presentation and add a final burst of herbaceous flavor.

## Variations and Dietary Substitutions
While the traditional Indian Butter Chicken Recipe is a meat-lover's delight, its core flavors can be adapted to suit various dietary needs and preferences.

*   **Vegetarian Butter "Chicken":** Replace chicken with paneer (Indian cottage cheese), tofu, or mixed vegetables like cauliflower, potatoes, and peas. Marinate paneer or tofu similarly, or simply pan-fry until golden before adding to the sauce.
*   **Vegan Butter "Chicken":** Use plant-based chicken substitutes, extra-firm tofu, or chickpeas. For the sauce, substitute butter with vegan butter or oil, and heavy cream with full-fat coconut milk or a cashew cream made from blended soaked cashews and water. Ensure your yogurt for marination is also plant-based.
*   **Gluten-Free:** This recipe is naturally gluten-free! Just ensure all your spices and ingredients are certified gluten-free, especially if using pre-made pastes or sauces.
*   **Healthier Options:** Reduce the amount of butter and cream, or opt for low-fat cream. Increase the vegetable content in the sauce by adding more pureed bell peppers along with tomatoes for extra nutrients and fiber.
*   **Spicier Kick:** If you prefer more heat, increase the amount of red chili powder or add a finely chopped green chili to the sauce while sautéing the onions.

There you have it – a comprehensive guide to preparing a truly authentic and delicious Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, right in your own kitchen. This beloved Indian lunch recipe is a testament to the country's rich culinary heritage, offering a symphony of flavors that is both comforting and exotic. By following this detailed Indian Butter Chicken Recipe, you can recreate the magic of a restaurant-quality dish, impressive enough for guests yet simple enough for a weeknight meal. So gather your ingredients, follow these steps, and prepare to delight your senses with one of India's most cherished culinary treasures. Enjoy the journey of cooking and savor every creamy, flavorful bite!
